aspect: SCENARIO - the citizenship that stops at the border
description: Nasrin becomes a Canadian citizen in 2025. Her Iranian nationality cannot be renounced in practice. If she enters Iran she enters as an Iranian, with no consular access. Her Canadian passport, which took nine years, is a document she cannot use in the one country she might need it.
energy_note: Nine years of work, void at one border.

description: Global Affairs Canada: avoid all travel; 'you should leave Iran now'. Canadians including dual Canadian-Iranian citizens are at high risk of arbitrary arrest and detention, and HOLDING A CANADIAN PASSPORT CAN BE REASON ENOUGH to detain you. Canada has no embassy or consulate in Iran.
energy_note: The passport you spent a decade earning is itself the risk factor.
source_name: Global Affairs Canada travel advice - Iran

description: Level 4 - Do Not Travel. Iran does not recognise dual nationality and treats US-Iranian dual nationals solely as Iranian citizens, and DUAL NATIONALS MUST EXIT IRAN ON IRANIAN PASSPORTS. Some US nationals have been held for years on false charges, tortured, and sentenced to death. As of 15 October 2025 routine consular services are no longer available.
energy_note: You may only leave on the passport that requires military clearance.
notes: Connects MIL-004 to STA-002: exit requires an Iranian passport, and an Iranian passport requires the service card.

description: Smartraveller: do not travel. Foreigners including Australians and dual nationals are at high risk of arbitrary detention, have been detained without due process, consular access and legal representation cannot be guaranteed, and THE AUSTRALIAN GOVERNMENT MAY NOT BE NOTIFIED of a detention at all.
energy_note: Detained, and nobody who could help is told.

description: Canada's advisory states plainly that Iranian authorities arrest and detain individuals 'including foreign and dual nationals, to exert political or diplomatic influence on their governments' - naming the practice as leverage rather than law enforcement.
